changelog: - **Broadcast and fan-out surfaces are tenant-scoped** (#2357, epic #2349). `Webhook`, `Announcement` and `Newsletter` gain a nullable `orgId` (backfilled to the default org by the schema-derived deploy backfill) and are registered with the tenant middleware — closing a latent cross-tenant leak that only bites once a second organization exists: `dispatchWebhook` filtered on `active` alone, so one tenant's `pipeline.stage_change` would fan out to another tenant's endpoint, and the newsletter dispatcher selected recipients by role across every tenant. Now `dispatchWebhook(event, data, orgId)` scopes to the acting tenant (threaded through all ten call sites — the acting user's org, or the relevant relation/mentor for the public and background paths), the newsletter dispatcher scopes recipients to the issue's own `orgId`, every create path stamps the creator's org (the curated-library cron issues to the default org), and the admin webhook endpoints (list, edit, delete, read) filter by the caller's org so one tenant's admin can neither see nor touch another's endpoints. The scoping is explicit rather than left to the middleware because these paths run fire-and-forget or from the cron, outside any request scope, and the middleware is advisory until `MT_ENFORCE_ISOLATION`. A no-op for today's single-tenant product (everything is the default org); a two-tenant e2e proves a tenant admin sees, edits and deletes only its own webhooks and that a created webhook is stamped with its org.
